cues.en: You are looking at a live view of the Falcon Heavy. Yes. The Falcon Heavy on historic Pad 39 A at Kennedy Space Center awaiting lift off at 03:45PM
cues.zh: 你看到的是 Falcon Heavy 的实时画面。没错，就是位于肯尼迪航天中心历史悠久的 39A 发射台、等待在下午 3:45 起飞的 Falcon Heavy

cues.en: local time.
cues.zh: 当地时间。

cues.en: Welcome to our live launch webcast. My name is Lauren Lyons. I'm an engineer in our flight reliability department here at SpaceX.
cues.zh: 欢迎收看我们的实时发射直播。我是 Lauren Lyons，是 SpaceX 飞行可靠性部门的工程师。

cues.en: I am so excited to be here with you today along with my cohost bringing you coverage of the first ever test flight of Falcon Heavy. At liftoff, Falcon Heavy is going to be the world's most powerful operational rocket by a factor of two. And today is the day that we attempt to demonstrate that power. And because it is a test flight, there is no satellite customer onboard the vehicle today, but the fairing is not empty.
cues.zh: 今天能和大家一起，为 Falcon Heavy 的首次试飞进行直播报道，我感到非常兴奋，我的搭档也会和我一起主持。这次起飞后，Falcon Heavy 将成为全球现役最强大的运载火箭，推力是第二名的两倍。今天，我们就要尝试证明它的实力。由于这是一次试飞，今天飞行器上没有卫星客户，但整流罩里并不是空的。

cues.en: We do have some very interesting payloads going up on this flight that we'll talk about later on in the webcast.
cues.zh: 这次飞行会搭载一些非常有意思的载荷，稍后我们会在直播中介绍。

cues.en: We'll also walk you through the mission profile because this ain't your typical Falcon launch. We've got 28 engines, three boosters, three separation events, three landing attempts, and there's gonna be a lot of activity happening all at once. So this test flight is bound to be exciting one way or another.
cues.zh: 我们也会带大家了解这次任务的飞行过程，因为这可不是一次普通的 Falcon 发射。我们有 28 台发动机、三个助推器、三次分离事件和三次着陆尝试，所有这些活动都会同时发生。因此，这次试飞无论如何都会非常精彩。

cues.en: Alright. We've got a ton to walk you through today, so let's get going.
cues.zh: 好了，今天有很多内容要带大家了解，我们开始吧。

cues.en: Hi. I'm Michael Hammersley, a materials engineer in the avionics department.
cues.zh: 大家好，我是 Michael Hammersley，航空电子部门的材料工程师。

cues.en: The...
We're very excited.
cues.zh: 我们非常期待。

cues.en: I'm sure you can hear it.
cues.zh: 我相信大家都能听到。

cues.en: To my right, we have a live view of Falcon Heavy on the pad at Kennedy Space Center.
cues.zh: 在我右侧，是 Falcon Heavy 位于肯尼迪航天中心发射台上的实时画面。

cues.en: Falcon Heavy is essentially
cues.zh: Falcon Heavy 本质上是

cues.en: three Falcon nine rockets all strapped together,
cues.zh: 三枚捆绑在一起的 Falcon 9 火箭，

cues.en: which means it can carry much larger payloads not only to Earth orbit but to the moon and Mars as well.
cues.zh: 这意味着它不仅能将更大的载荷送入地球轨道，还能送往月球和火星。

cues.en: So like Falcon nine, Falcon Heavy is a two stage launch vehicle.
cues.zh: 和 Falcon 9 一样，Falcon Heavy 也是两级运载火箭。

cues.en: The big difference is that the first stage in Falcon Heavy is comprised of three cores, while Falcon nine has only one. Now each one of these three cores has nine m one d engines,
cues.zh: 最大的区别在于，Falcon Heavy 的第一级由三个芯级组成，而 Falcon 9 只有一个。三个芯级中的每一个都配备九台 Merlin 1D 发动机，

cues.en: making for a total of 27 engines overall.
cues.zh: 总计 27 台发动机。

cues.en: Altogether, those engines produce 5,000,000
cues.zh: 这些发动机合计能产生 500 万

cues.en: pounds of thrust,
cues.zh: 磅推力，

cues.en: which is equal to eighteen seven forty sevens at takeoff. In fact, the engines are producing so much power that we don't run them at full thrust all at once. So during ascent, Falcon Heavy will throttle its thrust up and down in both the side and the center cores in order to balance the aerodynamic and structural loads on the vehicle.
cues.zh: 相当于起飞时同时使用 18 架 Boeing 747。实际上，这些发动机产生的动力非常强，所以我们不会让它们同时以满推力运行。因此在上升过程中，Falcon Heavy 会调高或调低两侧芯级和中央芯级的推力，以平衡飞行器所承受的气动载荷和结构载荷。

cues.en: So about halfway through the first stage's burn, the two side boosters will separate and come back to Earth for a simultaneous landing at Cape Canaveral Air Force Station. More
cues.zh: 因此，在第一级燃烧进行到大约一半时，两侧助推器会分离并返回地球，在卡纳维拉尔角空军基地同时着陆。稍后

cues.en: about that a bit later.
cues.zh: 我们会详细介绍这一点。

cues.en: At
cues.zh: 在

cues.en: that point,
cues.zh: 这一时刻，

cues.en: the mission proceeds very much like a standard Falcon nine flight. The center core will keep on firing for another minute to burn all of its fuel, and it will perform a standard stage separation from the second stage on top.
cues.zh: 任务的后续流程就和标准的 Falcon 9 飞行非常相似了。中央芯级会继续点火约一分钟，烧尽所有燃料，然后与顶部的第二级执行标准级间分离。

cues.en: This second stage, with the fairing right at the very top there, the second stage is exactly the same as any other Falcon nine flight, except we've loaded a bit more helium onto it this time. Now that second stage will be sending our payload way out into a Mars crossing orbit, which we'll also get into a bit later.
cues.zh: 这第二级，顶部正好有整流罩，除了这次装载了更多氦气外，和其他 Falcon 9 飞行任务的第二级完全相同。现在，这个第二级会把我们的载荷送入一条远至火星交会轨道的轨道，我们稍后也会详细介绍。

cues.en: But all in all, with a successful launch, Falcon Heavy is going to be the largest and most powerful operational rocket in the world. We're very excited to be launching it today. Let's check-in on exactly how it's doing.
cues.zh: 总的来说，只要发射成功，Falcon Heavy 将成为世界上最大、最强大的在役火箭。我们非常期待今天的发射。现在来看看它的具体状态。

cues.en: Good afternoon. I'm John Innsbrucker,
cues.zh: 下午好。我是 John Innsbrucker，

cues.en: the Falcon principal integration engineer
cues.zh: SpaceX 的 Falcon 首席集成工程师

cues.en: at SpaceX.
cues.zh: 目前在这里工作。

cues.en: We're currently at t minus seventeen minutes forty seconds and counting down. The good news that all systems are go for launch. We're working no problems with the SpaceX test flight of the Falcon Heavy launch vehicle.
cues.zh: 现在距离发射还有 17 分 40 秒，倒计时仍在继续。好消息是，所有系统都已准备就绪。Falcon Heavy 运载火箭的 SpaceX 测试飞行没有任何问题。

cues.en: Now we're currently loading propellant on all three first stage boosters,
cues.zh: 目前，我们正在给三个第一级助推器装载推进剂，

cues.en: and we began loading a couple minutes ago on the second stage of the LOX tank.
cues.zh: 几分钟前也开始给第二级的液氧罐装载液氧。

cues.en: Now this is the same method that we use on the single core Falcon nine. It just scaled to handle three first stage boosters.
cues.zh: 我们在单芯 Falcon 9 上采用的就是同样的方法，只是现在扩展到了三个第一级助推器。

cues.en: Now we're loading liquid oxygen and kerosene.
cues.zh: 现在我们正在装载液氧和煤油。

cues.en: We do that because in order to support combustion, you need oxygen. And in the vacuum of outer space, there isn't any. So we bring our own liquid oxygen,
cues.zh: 这是因为燃烧需要氧气，而外层空间是真空，没有氧气。所以我们要自带液氧，

cues.en: chilled and densified.
cues.zh: 并将其冷却、增密。

cues.en: You may have heard densified in the past. That allows us to patch the maximum
cues.zh: 你可能以前听说过“增密”这个词。这样可以让我们在 Falcon Heavy 的液氧罐中装入最大

cues.en: amount into the LOX tanks on the Falcon Heavy.
cues.zh: 容量的液氧。

cues.en: Now our fuel is refined petroleum,
cues.zh: 我们的燃料是精炼石油，

cues.en: RP one. That's essentially just a purified kerosene.
cues.zh: RP-1，本质上就是纯化后的煤油。

cues.en: It's a safe propellant, easily available, has a lot of history.
cues.zh: 这是一种安全、容易获得，而且拥有悠久使用历史的推进剂。

cues.en: For example, the Saturn five first stage flown from the very pad you see on the monitor
cues.zh: 例如，从你在监视器上看到的这个发射台发射、执行登月任务的土星五号第一级，

cues.en: from the moon missions used kerosene and liquid oxygen.
cues.zh: 使用的就是煤油和液氧。

cues.en: Now the big news this afternoon has been the weather and we've eaten up most of our launch window.
cues.zh: 今天下午的重大消息一直是天气，而我们已经耗掉了大部分发射窗口。

cues.en: Now we won't have the ability to hold the countdown any further now that we are into liquid oxygen loading. The good news is that the winds are looking good. We're working no issues on the Falcon Heavy.
cues.zh: 现在既然已经开始装载液氧，我们就无法再暂停倒计时了。好消息是，风况看起来不错。Falcon Heavy 目前没有任何问题。

cues.en: However, if there is an issue in the last minute, we won't be able to launch today. There is a backup date available tomorrow.
cues.zh: 不过，如果最后一分钟出现问题，我们今天就无法发射了。明天还有一个备用发射日期。

cues.en: I've said it before, launch is hard and Falcon Heavy is no exception.
cues.zh: 我以前说过，发射很难，Falcon Heavy 也不例外。

cues.en: We're essentially counting down three rockets simultaneously.
cues.zh: 我们实际上是在同时为三枚火箭倒计时。

cues.en: So the SpaceX team is going to be conservative
cues.zh: 因此，SpaceX 团队会采取保守策略，

cues.en: in case anything pops up in the last minutes.
cues.zh: 以防最后几分钟出现任何意外。

cues.en: But as the energy and the enthusiasm from the team gathering below me outside of Mission Control Center X is growing.
cues.zh: 不过，随着下方 Mission Control Center X 外聚集的团队越来越兴奋，现场的能量和热情也在不断高涨。

cues.en: We are go at t minus fifteen minutes and forty seconds and counting.
cues.zh: 现在是 T-15 分 40 秒，我们状态正常，倒计时继续。

cues.en: My name is Brian and I'm part of the software team here. And I'm standing just outside Mission Control as the crowd gathers behind me. We're all anxiously awaiting this very first test flight of Falcon Heavy. Now today, SpaceX has over 6,000 employees in locations across the country,
cues.zh: 我叫 Brian，是这里软件团队的一员。我现在就站在任务控制中心外，人群在我身后聚集。我们都在焦急等待 Falcon Heavy 的首次试飞。今天，SpaceX 在全国各地有超过 6000 名员工，

cues.en: but it wasn't always like that.
cues.zh: 但情况并非一直如此。

cues.en: Now when SpaceX was first founded in 2002,
cues.zh: SpaceX 最初成立于 2002 年时，

cues.en: was just a small group of engineers who believed that they could reduce the cost of exploring space but had never actually built a rocket themselves.
cues.zh: 只是一小群工程师，他们相信可以降低太空探索的成本，但自己从未真正造过火箭。

cues.en: Now Falcon one was the first rocket we developed, and it was pretty small relative to Falcon nine and Falcon Heavy.
cues.zh: Falcon one 是我们开发的第一枚火箭，相比 Falcon nine 和 Falcon Heavy，它相当小。

cues.en: While the Falcon Heavy on the right of your screen is over 230
cues.zh: 而你屏幕右侧的 Falcon Heavy 高超过 230

cues.en: feet tall, Falcon one stood only about 70 feet tall and could only carry about a half a ton to orbit.
cues.zh: 英尺，Falcon one 只有约 70 英尺高，最多只能把约半吨载荷送入轨道。

cues.en: However, despite its small size, Falcon one served a very large purpose. It was our roadmap to using modern technologies to engineer a vehicle that was not just more reliable,
cues.zh: 然而，尽管 Falcon one 体积小，它却承担了非常重要的使命。它是我们的路线图：用现代技术设计一种不仅更可靠、

cues.en: but was less expensive than alternatives.
cues.zh: 而且比替代方案更便宜的飞行器。

cues.en: Now we had three test flights of the Falcon one before we found success.
cues.zh: 在取得成功之前，我们进行了三次 Falcon one 试飞。

cues.en: But on that fourth Falcon one flight, it became the first privately developed liquid fueled rocket to reach Earth orbit.
cues.zh: 但在第四次 Falcon one 飞行中，它成为首枚由私人开发的液体燃料火箭进入地球轨道。

cues.en: Now fast forward to today and SpaceX has had 49 successful rocket launches. We have recovered twenty one first stages and we have reflown six of those. We have had 14 Dragon launches and have successfully reused the spacecraft as well.
cues.zh: 快进到今天，SpaceX 已成功进行 49 次火箭发射。我们回收了 21 个一级火箭，并已复飞其中 6 个。我们进行了 14 次 Dragon 发射，也成功复用了飞船。

cues.en: Now our next step on this journey is just minutes from now and we'll attempt the first test flight of our heavy lift launch vehicle.
cues.zh: 我们这段旅程的下一步就在几分钟后，我们将尝试首次试飞我们的重型运载火箭。

cues.en: Now there have been many challenges along this long road and it has not been easy. But no matter what happens today, it has all been worth it. Now one of the many challenges we're hoping to overcome with this test flight is the recovery of all three cores of the Falcon Heavy first stage. Although
cues.zh: 这一路走来有很多挑战，并不容易。但无论今天发生什么，这一切都值得。本次试飞我们希望克服的众多挑战之一，就是回收 Falcon Heavy 一级的全部三个芯级。虽然

cues.en: we have demonstrated success with the recovery of a single core, three is on a whole another level. So let's check-in with Michael to get an overview of what that story may look like.
cues.zh: 我们已成功回收单个芯级，但三个芯级完全是另一个层级。下面交给 Michael，请他概述一下可能的情况。

cues.en: At SpaceX, our primary goal is to enable people to live on other planets, most notably Mars.
cues.zh: 在 SpaceX，我们的首要目标是让人们能够生活在其他星球上，尤其是火星。

cues.en: But it's hard to do this without dramatically lowering the cost of access to space. And the best way to accomplish that is to reuse as much of the rocket as possible.
cues.zh: 但如果不大幅降低进入太空的成本，这很难实现。而做到这一点的最好方式，就是尽可能多地复用火箭。

cues.en: So we've been successful at landing and reusing Falcon nine rockets for over two years now, and Falcon Heavy aims to continue this trend of reusability.
cues.zh: 因此，我们已经成功着陆并复用 Falcon nine 火箭两年多，Falcon Heavy 旨在延续这种可复用趋势。

cues.en: So today, we'll be attempting to recover all three of the first stage cores by using both of our landing methods,
cues.zh: 所以今天，我们将尝试用两种着陆方式回收全部三个一级芯级，

cues.en: by land and by sea.
cues.zh: 陆地和海上。

cues.en: So the side boosters have actually been used before on missions Ticom eight and CRS nine.
cues.zh: 其实这些侧助推器此前已经在 Thaicom 8 和 CRS-9 任务中使用过。

cues.en: And at the time of booster separation during ascent, the side cores will still be going slowly enough to turn around. So it makes sense to return them to Cape.
cues.zh: 在上升段助推器分离时，侧芯级的速度仍足够慢，可以掉头返回。所以把它们送回卡纳维拉尔角是合理的。

cues.en: They'll be executing a three burn maneuver to get them back to Landing Zones 1 And 2 and Cape Canaveral Air Force Station.
cues.zh: 它们将执行三次点火机动，返回 1 号和 2 号着陆区以及卡纳维拉尔角空军基地。

cues.en: You may have heard of Landing Zone 1.
cues.zh: 你可能听说过 1 号着陆区。

cues.en: Landing Zone 2 is an identical landing pad right next to it for Falcon Heavy landings.
cues.zh: 2 号着陆区是紧挨着它的同款着陆坪，用于 Falcon Heavy 着陆。

cues.en: The SentraCore will be going too fast to efficiently return it to Cape Canaveral Air Force Station. So we're you... Going to use the autonomous spaceport drone ship to catch it about 300 miles off the Florida coast. It will also be executing three burns to get there.
cues.zh: 中央芯级速度会太快，无法高效返回卡纳维拉尔角空军基地。所以我们会……使用自主航天港无人船，在佛罗里达海岸约 300 英里外接住它。它也将执行三次点火来抵达那里。

cues.en: So if all goes well after launch, we'll have three first stage cores back on Earth, two for the second time, and a wealth of data for perfecting airplane like operation in the future.
cues.zh: 所以如果发射后一切顺利，我们将让三个一级芯级回到地球，其中两个是第二次使用，并获得大量数据，用于未来完善类似飞机的运营模式。

cues.en: So countdown is still proceeding nominally.
cues.zh: 倒计时仍在正常进行。

cues.en: So let's check-in again on how Falcon Heavy is doing.
cues.zh: 我们再来看一下 Falcon Heavy 的状态。

cues.en: We've just passed t minus 12 in the countdown of the test flight of Falcon Heavy.
cues.zh: 我们刚刚过了 Falcon Heavy 试飞倒计时的 T-12 分钟。

cues.en: Fuel is completely loaded on the second stage.
cues.zh: 二级燃料已完全加注完毕。

cues.en: The first stage is also loaded with fuel except for a small top off that'll happen between t minus seven minutes and t minus six minutes.
cues.zh: 一级也已加注燃料，只差少量补加，将在 T-7 到 T-6 分钟之间进行。

cues.en: Our major activity now is loading liquid oxygen on the boosters and the second stage.
cues.zh: 我们现在的主要工作是为助推器和二级加注液氧。

cues.en: Liquid oxygen propellant loading on the first stages will end between t minus four minutes and t minus three minutes.
cues.zh: 一级的液氧推进剂加注将在 T-4 到 T-3 分钟之间结束。

cues.en: Liquid oxygen loading on the second stage is the last one to finish, ending by t minus two minutes.
cues.zh: 二级的液氧加注是最后完成的，将在 T-2 分钟前结束。

cues.en: Now in addition to loading propellant, the team is preparing to perform their final checks of the Merlin engines.
cues.zh: 除了加注推进剂，团队还在准备对 Merlin 发动机进行最终检查。

cues.en: We'll begin chill in of the Merlin engine turbo pumps with liquid oxygen
cues.zh: 我们将开始用液氧对 Merlin 发动机涡轮泵进行预冷，

cues.en: as typical at T minus seven minutes like we do on Falcon nine flights.
cues.zh: 和 Falcon 9 飞行中一样，通常在 T-7 分钟进行。

cues.en: We'll also be verifying valves and using the thrust vector control actuators to move the engines to verify the actuators are working correctly.
cues.zh: 我们还会检查阀门，并使用推力矢量控制作动器转动发动机，以确认作动器工作正常。

cues.en: As we get to t minus four minutes, the clamp on the top of the strum back will open. You can see it just behind the Falcon Heavy. That entire structure will move about a degree and a half away from the rocket.
cues.zh: 到 T-4 分钟时，起竖架顶部的夹钳会打开。你能看到它就在 Falcon Heavy 后方。整个结构会从火箭旁移开约 1.5 度。

cues.en: At liftoff,
cues.zh: 在起飞时，

cues.en: it will move the rest of the way to clear Falcon Heavy just like Falcon Nine flights.
cues.zh: 它会继续移动，完全让开 Falcon Heavy，就像 Falcon 9 飞行中一样。

cues.en: At the t minus one minute mark, the flight computers will go into startup mode.
cues.zh: 到 T-1 分钟时，飞行计算机会进入启动模式。

cues.en: They'll be controlling the countdown on the Falcon Heavy.
cues.zh: 他们将负责控制 Falcon Heavy 的倒计时。

cues.en: What's different in this flight, engine ignition will begin at t minus five seconds on the two side boosters,
cues.zh: 这次飞行的不同之处在于，两枚侧助推器将在 T 减 5 秒时开始点火，

cues.en: followed two seconds later by the center core. Now we're continuing to watch the weather, making sure that the ground liftoff winds don't exceed maximum. They're looking good right now. We continue monitoring the upper altitude winds as reported by the balloons.
cues.zh: 两秒后，中心芯级也将点火。现在我们会继续关注天气，确保地面起飞风速不超过上限。目前情况看起来不错。我们还会继续监测气球报告的高空风速。

cues.en: But right now, at two minus ten minutes and ten seconds and counting, the Falcon Heavy test flight is go.
cues.zh: 不过现在，倒计时来到 T 减 2 分 10 秒，Falcon Heavy 测试飞行已获准发射。

cues.en: Because the first flight of Falcon Heavy is a test mission, we do not have a customer spacecraft on board today. Instead, we put something a little special to SpaceX inside the fairing. Now, more often than not, on the first flight of a new rocket, engineers would choose to fly a mass simulator, which is basically a heavy object of some sort to simulate the dynamics of flying a payload, but with little consequence if the mission doesn't work out exactly as planned. And as many of you already know, we have opted to have a little fun with our mass simulator.
cues.zh: 由于 Falcon Heavy 的首次飞行是一次测试任务，今天我们没有搭载客户的航天器。相反，我们在整流罩内放了一件对 SpaceX 来说颇为特别的东西。通常情况下，新火箭的首次飞行中，工程师会选择搭载质量模拟器，它基本上是某种重物，用来模拟搭载有效载荷飞行时的动力学特性；即使任务没有完全按计划进行，也不会造成太大损失。正如很多人已经知道的，我们决定让这个质量模拟器变得有趣一点。
